title: 1997 AMC 8 Problem 2
statement: Ahn chooses a two-digit integer, subtracts it from \(200,\) and doubles the result. What is the largest number Ahn can get?

solutions.text:
To get the largest number, we would want to subtract the smallest number possible from \(200.\)

The smallest two-digit number is \(10.\) Having Ahn choose this number will give us \[ 2 (200 - 10) = 2 \cdot 190 = 380 \] as the final result.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: To maximize the result, subtract the smallest possible two-digit number
